verdict.root_cause: The only positive failure signal on the board is in ad's own log: the OpenTelemetry Java agent cannot resolve the collector hostname, failing at DNS lookup before any socket or TLS handshake, persistently and recurring [tr_ddf22617dc70]. The process is alive — exporter threads still running, no startup, shutdown, or AdService-level exceptions — and early-window lines are clean request handling. Because ad's span metrics travel through that same collector, the intervals with no defined error ratio are best read as spans never arriving rather than ad refusing requests [tr_0621d82407a7, tr_5893dd7bbd5f]. frontend's span metrics are present and identically zero-errored in both windows, so the collector is reachable from frontend and the resolution failure is specific to ad [tr_c323a3e5240f]. No change is recorded for ad or flagd in the covered interval [tr_ef2799fd1927, tr_c3fd9efefcb9, tr_e82b0e0094fe], and the same process exported successfully earlier in the window, so a wrong endpoint value is not the mechanism. ad is running and its own log says it cannot reach what it needs.
verdict.reasoning: Freeze is excluded because ad writes continuously at the end of the window and shows no restart or shutdown banner [tr_ddf22617dc70]. bad_config is excluded because the same process exported cleanly earlier in the same window and no config push to ad is recorded [tr_ddf22617dc70, tr_c3fd9efefcb9] — a wrong endpoint value would have failed from start. frontend is excluded as originator: zero errored spans in both incident and baseline windows closes the sequencing argument [tr_c323a3e5240f]. The flat error ratio over the four hours ending at onset [tr_0621d82407a7] argues ad's request path was not itself failing; the metric gaps are downstream of the export failure rather than independent corroboration of an outage.
open_questions: Whether ad was actually still serving requests — request rate, latency, memory, and restart counts were never measured in any window [tr_0621d82407a7, tr_5893dd7bbd5f], so treating the metric gaps as an export artifact is inference, not observation.
Why frontend-proxy and load-generator alerted at 22:05:31; neither was dispatched, and frontend's zero errored spans does not account for those alerts.
Whether ad's loss of name resolution extends past the collector hostname to its own upstream dependencies — only the exporter path was observed failing.

alternatives.root_cause: ad's process is stopped or stalled while its socket still accepts, producing the traffic gaps and telemetry loss.
alternatives.why_not: A frozen process writes nothing; ad is emitting exporter stack traces throughout the late window [tr_ddf22617dc70].

alternatives.root_cause: ad's telemetry endpoint configuration names a collector hostname that does not resolve.
alternatives.why_not: The same process exported successfully earlier in the window and no config change to ad is recorded [tr_ddf22617dc70, tr_c3fd9efefcb9]; a wrong value would fail from startup.

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect should be observed. The board should stay as it is: ad's log continuing to emit OkHttp exporter stack traces that terminate in a DNS resolution failure for the collector hostname, and ad's span-metric series continuing to show undefined intervals, until a network-level reattachment is performed by a human or by an executor that has learned the reconnect class.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if ad's exporter failures stop on their own within the next several minutes without any network change — that would mean the resolution failure was transient and nothing needed doing. It is also wrong if someone measures ad's request rate, latency and restart count and finds the container has in fact been cycling (unobserved per tr_0621d82407a7 and tr_5893dd7bbd5f), which would move the mechanism from network to process state and make restart_service a legitimate proposal under its stated precondition. The fastest falsifier is the measurement that was never taken: ad container restart count and request rate over the incident window.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is that ad stays telemetry-blind and, if its loss of name resolution extends past the collector to flagd or its other upstreams (explicitly unresolved — only the exporter path was observed failing), it may also be failing real requests invisibly for as long as this sits unactioned. The risk I am declining to take is larger: restart_service is the only superficially plausible permitted action, its precondition is that evidence point at process state, and this evidence points at name resolution — tr_ddf22617dc70 rules out crash, restart and redeploy by the absence of any JVM startup or shutdown banner, and shows exporter threads alive at window end. Recreating a healthy container against a network-layer fault would discard its in-process cache, reset every in-flight gRPC call from frontend, and — if the container comes back attached to the same broken network state — leave the fault in place while consuming the one irreversible action available. rollback_image and revert_config are both precondition-blocked outright: the change log is empty for ad and for flagd across the covered interval (tr_ef2799fd1927, tr_c3fd9efefcb9), so there is no prior image tag or prior configuration to return to and no in-window change for either to undo.
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody sees a change, because nothing changes. The parties who remain affected are the ones already affected: ad itself, whose spans do not reach the collector; the observability pipeline, which keeps showing gaps for ad while frontend's series stay present and zero-errored (tr_c323a3e5240f), meaning the collector is reachable from frontend and this is ad-specific; and whoever is paging on frontend-proxy and load-generator at 22:05:31, whose alerts this abstention does not explain or clear. Escalate to an operator who can run the network reattachment directly — the world has performed it before — and in parallel ask for ad's request rate, latency, memory and restart counts, since the whole reading of the metric gaps as an export artifact rather than a service outage is inference and not yet observation.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts on ad and frontend-proxy with load-generator reflecting user-visible impact; nothing here is dismissible. flagd as a one-hop candidate cause makes a feature flag change a cheap first guess.
